Bangalore is steadily transforming into an urban area and it is therefore important as a tenant and employee to know the complexity involved in electricity billing. The electricity tariff structure is going to change in a big way in the year 2026 and will affect the costs people spend daily. This guide is extensive and goes into the revisited rates, government schemes and how Kots is going to ensure that it gets its residents transparent billing.

BESCOM's Revised Tariff Structure 2026: What Tenants Need to Know

Bangalore electricity supply company (BESCOM) has also introduced multi-year tariff change, which covers both the energy and fixed fees. The suggested increment is 74 paise per unit and an additional 91 paise per unit increment in 2026-27 and 2027-28 respectively. These are changes made in order to offset the increased price of power purchase and infrastructure upkeep.

Slab (Units) Previous Bangalore Electricity Rate (₹/unit) New Bangalore Electricity Rate (₹/unit)
0–50 5.00 5.74
51–100 5.50 6.24
101–200 6.00 6.74
201–300 6.50 7.24
Above 300 7.00 7.74

Note: Rates are indicative and subject to final approval by the Karnataka Electricity Regulatory Commission (KERC).

Gruha Jyothi Scheme: Free Electricity for Eligible Households

The Karnataka government provides the Gruha Jyothi scheme: Free Electricity , which offers free power to households with a monthly unit limit of 200. This will be an effort to mitigate the financial strain on the residents, such as tenants and workers. The state government requires households to register via the Seva Sindhu portal and meet certain criteria in order to be eligible.

Eligibility Criteria Details
Residential Status Must be a permanent resident of Karnataka
Household Type Domestic households only
Connection Type Must have an individual electricity connection (single meter)
Consumption Limit Eligible for free electricity up to 200 units per month
Income Criteria Household income must meet limits set by the state government (typically lower- to middle-income)
Registration Requirement Must register on the Seva Sindhu portal and provide valid documents
Excluded Groups Commercial establishments, industrial connections, and high-income households beyond specified limits

Impact on 9-to-5 Tenants: Managing Monthly Electricity Bills

The electricity consumption patterns of tenants are usually consistent with peak periods in case they are working a regular office schedule. Understanding the revised tariff structure enables better budgeting and energy management.

Employees who work 9-to-5 should follow this guideline to save some electricity.

  • Use energy efficient machines such as LED bulbs, inverter ACs and use energy saving fans.
  • Turn off appliances when not being used to prevent stand by power usage. Use the appliances only at off-peak times (early morning or after the day ends).
  • Use natural light and airing in the office when necessary to reduce use lighting and cooling requirements.
  • Periodic servicing of appliances to make them efficient.
  • Electronics can be automated to be switched off by using smart power strips or timers.

Smart Meters: A Step Towards Transparent Billing

BESCOM's smart metering project aims to initiate accurate real-time billing, thereby reducing the discrepancy between the bill and making it more transparent. Although the installation of smart meters is compulsory to new connections, the same does not necessarily apply to current tenants. Preparing for the future requires us to stay informed about this development.

Payment Options and Due Dates: Staying on Top of Your Bills

BESCOM provides different payment systems such as online portals, mobile apps, and physical payment centers. It is important that tenants become acquainted with these options and follow the billing plans so that the late charges and disruption of service do not occur. The auto-payment or reminder system can facilitate the payment procedure.

Troubleshooting Common Billing Issues

In some instances, tenants might experience irregularity between their electricity payment. The most common ones are the wrong meter readings, unoccupied period billing or the unexplained use. BESCOM's customer service should be immediately contacted by the tenants in such instances, or they should meet the nearest office to address the situation.

Tips for Reducing Electricity Consumption

Saving on energy will cause considerable savings. Changing lighting to LEDs, disconnecting unused appliances, and using programmable thermostats can help us save electricity. Also, every electrical appliance should be well maintained so that it is well-performing and uses less energy.

Conclusion: Navigating the 2026 Electricity Tariff Changes

The new model of electricity tariff in Bangalore requires active control of energy use and billing behavior. Tenants can maintain with the changes and implement energy saving measures in order to control their electricity costs. We at Kots, strive to provide our residents with clear and effective services, and ensure a comfortable life amidst changing challenges.

FAQs - Bangalore Electricity Rate per Unit in 2026

1. What is the Gruha Jyothi scheme, and how can I benefit from it?
The Gruha Jyothi scheme offers free electricity up to 200 units per month to eligible households in Karnataka. Tenants can register through the Seva Sindhu portal to avail of this benefit.
2. How can I calculate my monthly electricity bill under the new tariff structure?
Tenants can use BESCOM's online bill calculator or refer to the revised tariff slabs to estimate their monthly electricity costs based on their consumption.
3. Are there any rebates or discounts available for electricity consumers?
BESCOM provides a rebate of 25 paise per unit for households, schools, and hostels consuming electricity within specified limits.
4. What steps can I take to reduce my electricity consumption?
Adopting energy-efficient practices, such as using LED lighting, unplugging unused appliances, and optimizing usage during off-peak hours, can help reduce electricity consumption.
5. What is the per-unit electricity rate in Bangalore for 2026?
Details on the revised BESCOM rates for different slabs.
6. How do smart meters impact my electricity bills?
